quote.text: The problem, Paulinus, is not that we have a short life, but that we waste time. Life is long and there is enough of it for satisfying personal accomplishments if we use our hours well. But when time is squandered in the pursuit of pleasure or in vain idleness, when it is spent with no real purpose, the finality of death fast approaches and it is only then, when we are forced to, that we, at last, take a good hard look at how we have spent our life- just as we become aware that it is ending. Thus the time we are given is not brief, but we make it so. We do not lack time; on the contrary, there is so much of it that we waste an awful lot
quote.author: Seneca the elder
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • Consider that each moment spent with your children is a chance to instill wisdom and character—wasting time is akin to squandering the opportunity to shape their future with purpose and virtue.
    • Just as time is a resource not measured by its length but by its use, invest in meaningful interactions that nurture resilience and help your children understand the value of every hour.
  • Leadership:
    • A leader must recognize that time is a tool; every decision and action should be deliberate and purposeful, ensuring that the collective journey towards success is neither aimless nor wasted.
    • By modeling disciplined and mindful time management, you inspire others to seek fulfillment through genuine accomplishments rather than fleeting pleasures or idle distractions.
  • Product Management:
    • In product management, the fleeting nature of time reminds us to focus on value-driven actions—prioritize tasks that contribute meaningfully to the end goal rather than getting lost in non-essential details.
    • Embrace a mindset that sees every sprint, every iteration as an opportunity: when time is managed with purpose, innovation thrives and real progress becomes evident.
